title: Visual Quality Inspection on Production Lines
summary: Cameras and vision models at the inspection station flag scratches, dents, missing features and print errors, divert clear rejects and hold borderline parts for an inspector.

seo.title: AI Visual Inspection for Production Lines | VipraTech
seo.description: Vision models at the line flag surface defects, missing features and print errors, divert rejects via the PLC and hold borderline parts for inspectors.

problem.intro: Most plants still rely on inspectors at the end of the line, checking parts under a lamp against limit samples. It works until volumes rise, shifts change or a new variant arrives, and then defects reach the customer's incoming inspection.

pain_points.title: Inspector fatigue and drift
pain_points.detail: Detection of small scratches, burrs or short shots varies by inspector, by shift and by the hour of the shift.

pain_points.title: Escapes found by the customer
pain_points.detail: Defects that slip through come back as line rejections, sorting at the customer's site and 8D reports that consume the quality team.

pain_points.title: Brittle rule-based vision
pain_points.detail: Older vision systems tuned with fixed thresholds break with lighting changes, part variants and reflective surfaces, so operators put them in bypass.

pain_points.title: No image record for traceability
pain_points.detail: When a complaint arrives, there is no picture of how that serial or batch looked when it left the line.

solution.overview: We build an inspection station around your part: camera, lens, lighting and trigger chosen for the defect classes that matter, and models trained on your good parts and real defects. The model scores each part against your defect library and returns pass, fail or uncertain within the station's cycle time. Clear failures go to the NG bin through a PLC signal. Uncertain parts are held for an inspector instead of being passed. Every image is stored against the part serial or batch, so quality engineers get a defect Pareto by shift and a visual record for customer complaints.
capabilities: Detects surface defects such as scratches, dents, porosity, burrs, paint runs and short shots
Checks presence and position of features such as holes, clips, fasteners, O-rings and labels
Reads printed date codes, batch numbers and part markings for legibility and correctness
Anomaly model trained on good parts to catch defect types not yet in the library
Sends reject signals to the PLC over digital I/O or OPC UA within the station cycle time
Stores every image with its verdict, part serial, model version and shift

workflow.title: Trigger at the station
workflow.detail: A photo-sensor or PLC signal fires the camera when the part is in position under controlled lighting.

workflow.title: Capture images
workflow.detail: One or more cameras capture the part from the agreed angles, with a quick check for blur or glare.

workflow.title: Score against the defect library
workflow.detail: Detection and anomaly models score the images for each defect class agreed with the quality team.

workflow.title: Decide pass, fail or uncertain
workflow.detail: Clear passes continue, clear fails are diverted to the NG bin, and anything in between is held.

workflow.title: Inspector review of held parts
workflow.detail: An inspector checks held parts at the rework station against limit samples and records the verdict.

workflow.title: Log and trace
workflow.detail: The image, verdict, part serial, model version and shift are written to the traceability store.

workflow.title: Analyse and improve
workflow.detail: Quality engineers review the defect Pareto, label new examples and approve model updates.

inputs: Images from line cameras at the inspection station
Golden samples and limit samples agreed with quality
Labelled defect images from past rejections and rework
Part serial or batch data from MES or barcode
Defect classes and acceptance criteria from the control plan
outputs: Pass, fail or hold verdict per part within the cycle time
Reject signal to the PLC for NG diversion
Image record per part serial with verdict and model version
Defect Pareto by class, shift and line
Labelled examples for the next model update
human_in_the_loop: Inspectors decide every part the model holds as uncertain, using the same limit samples they use today. Quality engineers approve each model update and any change to defect classes, and line-stop decisions stay with the shift supervisor.
integrations: PLC via digital I/O, fieldbus gateway or OPC UA
MES or traceability system for part serials
Plant network storage or a private cloud bucket for images
Andon or line display for alerts
guardrails: Uncertain parts are held for an inspector, never passed by default
Shift-start check with golden and known-defect samples
Model version recorded against every verdict, with rollback
Alerts when lighting, focus or camera position drifts
Camera framing limited to the part, not operators
compliance_notes: Inspection images and verdicts can serve as evidence for ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 traceability records; the quality system and its controls stay with you.
Cameras are framed on parts so the system does not process images of workers.

pilot.scope: One inspection station, one part family and the three to five defect classes that cause most rejections, run in shadow mode next to manual inspection.
deliverables: Camera, lens and lighting specification for the station
Trained models for the agreed defect classes
Inspector review screen and image log
Comparison report against inspector verdicts on the same parts
Line roll-out plan with hardware and cost estimate

faqs.q: How many defect images do we need to start?
faqs.a: Fewer than most teams expect, because the anomaly model learns from good parts and flags anything unusual. For each named defect class we collect real examples from rejection bins and rework during the pilot. Rare defects stay with the anomaly model and the inspector until enough examples exist.

faqs.q: Can it keep up with our line speed?
faqs.a: The model runs on edge hardware next to the station, so there is no round trip to the cloud. We size the camera, lens and compute to your cycle time during the pilot and report the measured time per part.

faqs.q: Will it work on shiny, oily or dark parts?
faqs.a: Reflective and oily surfaces are mostly a lighting problem. We choose dome, low-angle or polarised lighting for the defect type and test on your real parts before you commit to hardware.

faqs.q: Do our images leave the plant?
faqs.a: Not unless you want them to. Inference and image storage can stay on the plant network, with only summary data sent to a dashboard. Model training can also run on-premise.
